items.claim: Ezek.44.1-44.4 holds one literary movement and not two: the guide's movement verb at 44.1 reopens the vision frame at the shut outer east gate, 44.2-3 give the gate's meaning and the prince's privilege, and 44.4 is a second movement of the same guided scene, ending on the glory filling the house and the prostration that is this book's vision-close gesture, borne by 5 verses in all (1.28, 3.23, 11.13, 43.3, 44.4). The competing division that would attach 44.4 to the statute is weaker because 44.4 carries no statute diction and the instructional mode does not begin until the address at 44.5.
items.both_sides: Close side of the row's own seam: 44.4 ends on the prostration after the glory is seen, and there is no statute language anywhere in 44.1-44.4. Onset side: 44.5 opens with the address to the son of man and the directive to attend to the ordinances and entrances of the house, which changes the mode from narrated vision to statute; it is one of only 2 son-of-man addresses in chs 44-48 (44.5, 47.6) per the device census. Behind the row's own onset, the witness records a doubled setumah on 43.27, so the opening seam is marked on its far side as well. The row argues from 43.27 in prose without mirroring it in its structured evidence list; this does not damage the form argument, because the onset carries its own cited device at 44.1.

suggested_fix.fact: no boundary change; optionally mirror the closing mark behind the onset in the structured evidence, since the prose already argues from it

items.claim: The boundary is right, but the row asserts a book-wide digit that is wrong for the object it names: it calls Ezek.45.17 one of four verses in the book carrying the construction glossed at the new moons, while naming only one companion. Swept over the Hebrew witness on the accent-stripped skeleton, that construction stands on 2 verses (45.17, 46.3). The digit 4 belongs to a different object, the bare plural month-word, which stands on 4 verses (39.12, 39.14, 45.17, 46.3) — and 2 of those 4 are the burial durations of the Gog passage, not new moons at all. Two swept objects are blended under one count, which the corpus's count discipline forbids.
items.both_sides: Close side: 45.17 ends the prince's duty for the offerings at the appointed times and the witness records a SAMEKH there. Onset side: 45.18 opens with a messenger formula, which with a marked close standing behind it satisfies the condition for cutting at a messenger formula; the subject also turns from measures and dues to the sanctuary's annual purgation. The internal split the row rejects, at 45.12/45.13, has no onset device: the device census places the chapter's only messenger formulae at 45.9 and 45.18, so nothing opens a unit at 45.13.

suggested_fix.fact: name the swept object before the digit and count that object alone: the at-the-new-moons construction stands on 2 verses, and the bare plural month-word on 4, of which the two outside this part are burial durations rather than new moons

The four month-and-day dates the span covers (45.18, 45.20, 45.21, 45.25) carry no year word, so none meets the structural dateline test and none opens a unit; the row states that denial as its own proposition with the test that grounds it, namely a year word together with a month or day term, rather than leaving it as an aside. Checked against the device census, those four verses are exactly its calendar-dates-that-are-not-datelines class, and none of the 14 year-bearing datelines falls at or after 44.1.

items.claim: Ezek.46.16-46.18 is a coherent three-verse inheritance statute and both its seams fall in the right place, but the row states the wrong warrant for its onset: it calls a distinct subject exactly the corroboration required before a messenger-formula seam is honoured, whereas the ruled condition is an addressee change or a refrain-grade close immediately before, and 46.15 carries no close formula of any class. The available corroboration is the PE recorded on 46.15, which informs and cannot decide alone, together with the turn from second-person offering instruction to third-person casuistic law. Both of this row's seam warrants, the mark at 46.15 and the movement verb at 46.19, are argued in prose and absent from its structured evidence, so the row's close rests entirely on a verse it never cites as evidence.
items.both_sides: Onset side: 46.16 carries a fresh messenger formula and turns to the prince's gifts to sons and servants, casuistic third-person law after the second-person offering instruction of 46.13-15. Close side: 46.18 ends the prohibition on the prince taking the people's holding, and 46.19 carries a movement verb that reopens the guided vision scene, a unit-class change from statute to vision narrative; the witness records no mark on 46.16, 46.17 or 46.18, so the close does rest on that class change, as the row says. The device census places no close formula at 46.15, which is why the messenger formula at 46.16 cannot be honoured on the ruled refrain-close limb and must be carried on the mark and the class shift instead.

suggested_fix.fact: state the warrant as it stands: no close formula falls on the verse before this onset, so the corroboration is the parashah mark recorded there, single-witness and non-deciding, together with the shift from second-person offering instruction to third-person casuistic law; and carry both that mark and the movement verb at the far side of the close into the structured evidence

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the argued-but-unmirrored pattern should be read as a per-row defect or as a corpus-level convention. It stands on 6 of this cluster's 8 rows and on 115 of the 145 rows corpus-wide, so it is systemic rather than local. This review therefore charged it only where the unmirrored verse carries a whole seam warrant, at the onset at 45.1 and at both seams of the statute at 46.16-46.18, and named it without charging it where the seam has its own cited device, at the onsets at 44.1, 45.9, 45.18 and 46.1.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: If the convention is that adjacent-verse warrants live in prose by design, then two of this review's four challenges narrow to their disclosure limbs; if it is a defect, the same pattern is owed a corpus-wide order rather than eight row-level fixes.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the 14-16 verse allowance extends by its reasoning to statute chapters, or is closed to the measured and listed blocks it names. Two rows here run past the 7-10 target (17 verses at 44.15-44.31 and 15 at 46.1-46.15) and both cite that allowance; on the closed reading neither may, though each is genuinely uncuttable for want of an internal onset device.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: It decides whether the length disclosures on those two rows are correct as written or need restating against the ruled target, and it is the same question for every long statute row in this part.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether 44.4 belongs with the vision scene above it or heads the statute below it. This review reads it with the scene, on the movement verb and the prostration, and the row is supported on that reading; the alternative division is disclosed by the row and is not unreasonable.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: It is the only seam in this cluster where two readings both rest on real devices rather than on one reading resting on an absence.

Every file I opened was named by exact path in my launch message or my brief, plus the governance ledger that my launch message named by exact path. I read nothing from the other lane, no other reviewer's output, no fix-up order, no cure claim, no ruling and no transcript. My private working file lives in a uniquely named subdirectory of my own session scratchpad, and I wrote nothing under the worktree.
